es.summary: La deficiencia de dopamina es la disminución de este neurotransmisor en los ganglios basales, provocando trastornos del movimiento como la enfermedad de Parkinson y la distonía.
key_points: Se relaciona con pérdida de neuronas en la sustancia negra.
El tratamiento busca restaurar el equilibrio dopamina‑acetilcolina.
El manejo incluye fármacos dopaminérgicos y terapia física.
Riesgo elevado de caídas y pérdida de autonomía.

pathophysiology: La dopamina se sintetiza en la sustancia negra del mesencéfalo.
Su deficiencia reduce la inhibición del núcleo subtalámico.
Aumenta la actividad del circuito indirecto, generando hiperactividad inhibidora del tálamo.
Resultado: disminución del movimiento voluntario y contracciones musculares anormales.
signs_symptoms: Bradicinesia y dificultad para iniciar movimientos.
Rigidez muscular y temblor en reposo.
Fatiga y disminución de la resistencia a la actividad.
diagnostics: DAT‑scan muestra disminución de captación de dopamina.
Resonancia magnética para descartar otras causas.
No existen pruebas de laboratorio específicas.
complications: Pérdida de autonomía en actividades de la vida diaria.
nursing_care: Evaluar fuerza muscular, tono y marcha en cada turno.
Monitorear efectos de la medicación (dyskinesias, hipotensión ortostática).
Implementar medidas de prevención de caídas (pasamanos, calzado antideslizante).
Asistir al paciente en ADL, fomentando la independencia.
Registrar horarios de medicación y respuesta clínica.
patient_teaching: Tomar levodopa con el estómago vacío y evitar alimentos ricos en proteínas al mismo tiempo.
Importancia de la adherencia al esquema de medicación.
Ejercicios de estiramiento y entrenamiento de equilibrio diarios.
Señales de alerta: aumento de temblor, caídas o confusión.
Uso de dispositivos de apoyo (bastón, andador) según indicación.

outcomes: Nivel de tolerancia a la actividad: aumentar a 30 min sin fatiga en 2 semanas
Capacidad para realizar ADL: independiente en al menos 4 de 6 actividades en 4 semanas

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y capacidad funcional antes y después de la actividad.
interventions.rationale: Permite establecer la línea base y medir la mejora.

interventions.action: Planificar actividades en intervalos cortos con descansos programados.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la fatiga y mejora la tolerancia gradual.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (sentarse para vestirse, usar apoyos).
interventions.rationale: Facilita la realización de tareas sin sobrecargar al paciente.

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapia para ejercicios de fortalecimiento y movilidad.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la fuerza muscular y la resistencia.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de sobreesfuerzo (taquicardia, sudoración).
interventions.rationale: Previene complicaciones relacionadas con la intolerancia.

outcomes: Incidencia de caídas: cero durante la hospitalización
Lesiones relacionadas con caídas: ninguna en 30 días

interventions.action: Realizar evaluación de riesgo de caídas al ingreso y cada 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifica cambios en el estado motor que aumenten el riesgo.

interventions.action: Mantener el entorno libre de obstáculos y bien iluminado.
interventions.rationale: Reduce oportunidades de tropiezos.

interventions.action: Proveer dispositivos de apoyo (bastón, andador) según necesidad.
interventions.rationale: Mejora la estabilidad al caminar.

interventions.action: Instruir al paciente sobre levantarse lentamente para evitar hipotensión ortostática.
interventions.rationale: Previene desmayos y caídas súbitas.

interventions.action: Registrar y reportar cualquier episodio de caída o pérdida de equilibrio.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la intervención temprana y ajuste del plan de cuidados.

en.summary: Dopamine deficiency is the reduction of this neurotransmitter in the basal ganglia, causing movement disorders such as Parkinson’s disease and dystonia.
key_points: Associated with loss of neurons in the substantia nigra.
Treatment aims to restore the dopamine‑acetylcholine balance.
Management includes dopaminergic drugs and physical therapy.
High risk of falls and loss of autonomy.

pathophysiology: Dopamine is synthesized in the substantia nigra of the midbrain.
Its deficiency reduces inhibition of the subthalamic nucleus.
It increases activity of the indirect circuit, producing inhibitory hyperactivity of the thalamus.
Result: decreased voluntary movement and abnormal muscle contractions.
signs_symptoms: Fatigue and reduced endurance for activity.
diagnostics: Clinical evaluation with the UPDRS scale.
DAT scan shows decreased dopamine uptake.
MRI to rule out other causes.
complications: Loss of autonomy in activities of daily living.
nursing_care: Assess muscle strength, tone, and gait each shift.
Implement fall prevention measures (handrails, non‑slip footwear).
Assist the patient with ADLs, encouraging independence.
Document medication times and clinical response.
patient_teaching: Take levodopa on an empty stomach and avoid protein‑rich foods at the same time.
Daily stretching and balance training exercises.
Warning signs: increased tremor, falls, or confusion.
Use assistive devices (cane, walker) as indicated.

outcomes: Activity tolerance level: increase to 30 min without fatigue in 2 weeks
Ability to perform ADLs: independent in at least 4 of 6 activities in 4 weeks

interventions.action: Assess energy level and functional capacity before and after activity.
interventions.rationale: Establishes baseline and measures improvement.

interventions.action: Plan activities in short intervals with scheduled rest periods.
interventions.rationale: Reduces fatigue and improves gradual tolerance.

interventions.action: Teach energy conservation techniques (sit to dress, use supports).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates task completion without overloading the patient.

interventions.action: Coordinate with physical therapy for strengthening and mobility exercises.
interventions.rationale: Improves muscle strength and endurance.

interventions.action: Monitor signs of overexertion (tachycardia, sweating).
interventions.rationale: Prevents complications related to intolerance.

interventions.action: Perform fall risk assessment upon admission and every 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifies changes in motor status that increase risk.

interventions.action: Keep the environment free of obstacles and well lit.
interventions.rationale: Reduces tripping opportunities.

interventions.action: Provide assistive devices (cane, walker) as needed.
interventions.rationale: Improves stability while walking.

interventions.action: Instruct the patient to rise slowly to avoid orthostatic hypotension.
interventions.rationale: Prevents fainting and sudden falls.

interventions.action: Document and report any fall or loss of balance episode.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early intervention and care plan adjustment.

key_points.0.quote: Evaluate therapeutic effects—decrease in drooling, tremors, bradykinesia, or rigidity and increase in facial expressions.

key_points.2.quote: Drugs are given to restore the balance of dopamine and ACh in certain areas of the brain.

key_points.3.quote: Doctors use medicines, Botox injections, surgery, physical therapy, and other treatments to reduce or eliminate muscle spasms and pain.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Evaluate therapeutic effects—decrease in drooling, tremors, bradykinesia, or rigidity and increase in facial expressions.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Increased muscle tone with cogwheel rigidity in upper extremities. Neurological: Resting tremor in right hand.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Dystonia is a movement disorder that causes involuntary contractions of your muscles.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Monitor serum liver enzymes, hemoglobin/hematocrit, bilirubin, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), Coombs tests, and elevated serum glucose periodically throughout treatment.

sections.treatment.0.quote: This is beneficial, not only to increase the amount of dopamine that reaches the brain, but also to diminish the adverse effects dopamine causes when circulating in the periphery.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Do not confuse ropinirole ( dopamine agonist ) with risperidone ( antipsychotic ).

sections.treatment.2.quote: Safinamide: A reversible MAO-B inhibitor that inhibits voltage-sensitive sodium channels and glutamate release.

sections.treatment.3.quote: Entacapone: A selective, reversible COMT inhibitor for the treatment of PD.

sections.treatment.5.quote: Engage in physical therapy to increase balance and strength.

sections.complications.2.quote: About 80% of clients treated with levodopa will experience drug-induced dyskinesias during the advanced stages of the disease, and 30% will develop it after only 3 years of levodopa treatment (Kwon et al., 2022).

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: This drug should be taken on an empty stomach, typically 30 minutes before a meal.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: The combination form increases adherence because the client only needs to take one drug versus two different ones.
